title: Book Launch Checklist
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Intelligent Textbook Publishing
Book Launch Checklist
Deployment Verification
Book Metrics
Announcements
description: Top-to-bottom checklist flowchart of the seven steps before a book is announced: strict build passes, deployment verified live, book-metrics.json regenerated, README regenerated from metrics, announcement drafted, announcement preview image checked, and publish. For each step the reader chooses between a sound and an unsound reason for doing it before the next step. A sound reason checks the step off; clicking a step out of order explains what the skipped step protects. Publish unlocks after all six confirmations.

educational.topic: Ordering and justifying the confirmations before a book announcement
learningObjectives: Justify why each launch-checklist item must pass before an announcement goes out, in the correct order.
Distinguish a sound reason for a step's position from a plausible but unsound one.
Explain what goes wrong when a checklist step is taken out of order.
prerequisites: Has read about strict build mode and deployment verification
Has read about the book-metrics.json hub and the canonical metrics principle
Knows what a README and a social media preview card are

controls.label: Checklist node
controls.description: Each of the seven nodes has a Mermaid click directive. The next unchecked step opens a question with two candidate reasons; a checked step shows its justification; a later step explains why it cannot be done yet

controls.label: Candidate reason
controls.description: Two answer buttons per step: the sound reason checks the step off, the unsound one gives corrective feedback

controls.label: Next Step
controls.description: Opens the next unchecked step, the same as clicking its node; becomes Publish when all six confirmations are checked

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Clears every check mark and returns to the overview

controls.label: Tab and Enter
controls.description: Nodes and buttons can be focused with Tab and selected with Enter or Space

pedagogical.pattern: Ordered checklist with judged justifications and feedback
pedagogical.teachingStrategy: The learner evaluates two candidate reasons for each step's position, receives feedback, and sees the consequence of taking steps out of order
keyQuestions: What does the next step depend on that this step provides?
What would a first reader experience if this step were skipped?
commonMisconceptions: The announcement copies its numbers from the README
A clean local build proves the live site works
The order of the last few steps does not matter
assessmentOpportunities: Write the seven steps in order from memory with a one-sentence justification for each
Explain what is wrong with each rejected reason
